title: Guilt, Power and Honest Gain
overview: A collection of short sayings contrasting honest and crooked people, especially in how they handle guilt, power and money.

parts.label: Guilt, fear and confession (vv. 1, 13-14, 17)
parts.note: A guilty conscience makes people jumpy even when no one is chasing them, while those with nothing to hide can face trouble boldly, and hiding wrongs goes badly while admitting and dropping them meets mercy. Verse 17 pictures a killer weighed down by guilt, and scholars are unsure whether it means others should not shield him from justice or simply that his guilt will drive him to ruin.

parts.label: Good and bad rulers (vv. 2-3, 12, 15-16, 28)
parts.note: A land in moral trouble churns through leaders, and a ruler who squeezes the poor is like a flooding rain that ruins the crops (the Hebrew of verse 3 may instead mean a poor man who oppresses the poor). When the wicked take power people hide, and when they fall, good people flourish again.

parts.label: Listening to God's teaching (vv. 4-5, 7, 9-10, 18, 26)
parts.note: The word for instruction here means God's teaching or law, and the sayings link following it with seeing clearly what is right. Verse 9 goes further than calling prayer useless: if someone refuses to listen to that teaching, even their prayers are called detestable, and verse 26 calls trusting only your own judgment foolish.

parts.label: Wealth, honest and crooked (vv. 6, 8, 11, 19-22)
parts.note: Israel's law forbade charging interest on loans to poor neighbors, and verse 8 says such gains will end up with someone who is kind to the poor. Honest work and integrity count for more than quick riches, which these sayings tie to cheating, a stingy heart, and doing wrong for as little as a piece of bread.

parts.label: Greed, family and the poor (vv. 23-25, 27)
parts.note: Honest correction earns more thanks in the end than flattery, and anyone who takes from their own parents while saying it is not wrong is no better than a destroyer. Greed stirs up fights, those who give to the poor do not go without, and those who look away earn many curses.

think: In your experience, does keeping something hidden change how a person carries themselves, even if no one else ever finds out?
